$$
u=- 5 x\qquad v=y\qquad w=z.
$$" :question/worked-solution "For a transformation

$$
T:(u,v,w)\to(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)),
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T$ is $\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}$.

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}$, the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$.

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=-5 & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=0 & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z}=0 \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=0 & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y}=1 & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z}=0 \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x}=0 & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y}=0 & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\begin{vmatrix}-5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=-5\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=-5\left(1\cdot 1-0\right) \\ &=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}&=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1} \\ &=- \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["2eb6301b-47d8-5a7f-8598-fe21b9f7e95c"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "1b9d74b8-e21a-5070-b867-4bb5e1c969bb" :answer/id #uuid "1b9d74b8-e21a-5070-b867-4bb5e1c969bb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "044ebbb0-49a4-5e07-aa5f-52071f46d7bb" :answer/id #uuid "044ebbb0-49a4-5e07-aa5f-52071f46d7bb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "- \frac{1}{6}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "fa3f7b1e-e9e6-5da0-a816-27f38a49b857" :answer/id #uuid "fa3f7b1e-e9e6-5da0-a816-27f38a49b857" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{36}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "2d993ae9-8ed2-5193-82c6-1154b2659b11" :answer/id #uuid "2d993ae9-8ed2-5193-82c6-1154b2659b11" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "6" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "7fcacf0f-5374-5915-8bc2-3f0e72e2b38a" :answer/id #uuid "7fcacf0f-5374-5915-8bc2-3f0e72e2b38a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{6}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "dabd80d4-e1e0-5326-9f3e-7bad3d5ea123" :answer-field/id #uuid "dabd80d4-e1e0-5326-9f3e-7bad3d5ea123" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/choices ["1b9d74b8-e21a-5070-b867-4bb5e1c969bb" "044ebbb0-49a4-5e07-aa5f-52071f46d7bb" "fa3f7b1e-e9e6-5da0-a816-27f38a49b857" "2d993ae9-8ed2-5193-82c6-1154b2659b11" "7fcacf0f-5374-5915-8bc2-3f0e72e2b38a"] :answer-field/correct "7fcacf0f-5374-5915-8bc2-3f0e72e2b38a" :db/ensure :answer-field/validate} {:db/id "911ff483-5437-5b63-bdea-c53a9f75354d" :question/id #uuid "911ff483-5437-5b63-bdea-c53a9f75354d" :question/problem "Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))$, given that

$$

$$

Scaling the three derivative rows by $3, 3, 2$ multiplies the determinant by $18$.

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}3\left({e}^{x}\right) & 0 & 0 \\ 3\left({e}^{x+y}\right) & 3\left({e}^{x+y}\right) & 0 \\ 2\left({e}^{x+y+z}\right) & 2\left({e}^{x+y+z}\right) & 2\left({e}^{x+y+z}\right)\end{vmatrix} \\  & =18\left({e}^{x}\begin{vmatrix}{e}^{x+y} & 0 \\ {e}^{x+y+z} & {e}^{x+y+z}\end{vmatrix}\right)\\  & =18\left({e}^{x}({e}^{2x+2y+z}-0)\right)\\  & =18 e^{x} e^{x + y} e^{x + y + z}.\end{aligned}
